All walkthroughs / Harbour Clinic

Harbour Clinic · Closing an organisation

Close down an organisation, and keep its records for a legal case

A small clinic is closing down. Its data custodian starts the closing down, and an ordinary member is refused when trying to stop it. After 15 days nobody in the clinic can do anything. A law firm asks that the records be kept, so one platform administrator records a legal hold and a different one approves it. Everything inside the clinic is deleted only after the hold is released, and a short record says that it was.

5People

How to read this page

  • Every step is one screen, or one moment, in a real run. The label under the title names where it happens, and the step reads in the same order each time: what is happening, the evidence, and then what to look for in it.
  • Screenshots are real pictures of the Munitas console, the web app that people open in a browser. Click any picture to enlarge it.
  • Every name of a person, patient or card holder in the example data is invented, and every screenshot is unedited apart from being cropped to the part that matters.

Words used on this page

Organisation
A company or hospital group that uses Munitas. Each organisation sees only its own data.
Department
A team inside an organisation that owns some of its data, such as Cardiology.
Dataset
A named collection of records, such as a table of patient admissions.
Custodian
A person who holds the data custodian role, which allows deciding who may read data. A custodian decides for the departments they are an approver for.
Role
A named set of permissions that a person can hold, such as the permission to decide who may read a department’s data.
Platform administrator
The person who runs Munitas itself. The role gives no say over who may read any department’s data.
Closing down an organisation
Ending an organisation’s use of Munitas in two stages of 15 days. In the first its people can read and may cancel. In the second they can do nothing. When both end, everything inside the organisation is deleted.
Legal hold
An instruction from a court, a regulator or a law firm to keep an organisation’s records and not delete them while a legal matter is open.
Temporary custodian
The person a legal hold names to answer for the kept records while the hold stands. The person confirms having read the notice.
Data protection officer
A person who watches how an organisation handles personal data. The role decides nothing about who may read it.
Sweep
The check that Munitas makes every few minutes for organisations whose time is up. It deletes an organisation only when both periods have ended and no legal hold stands.
Sealed
Finished and closed for good, so that it can never be edited.
Claim
A statement, made by the person who brings a dataset in, about how sensitive it is. A different approver of the owning department has to confirm it.
Version
One sealed state of a dataset. Changing the contents means making a new version, never editing an old one.
Release
A decision to let a dataset version be read more widely than before. A release changes who may read it and moves no data.

PART ONE

The data custodian closes the clinic down

Harbour Clinic is a small clinic that is closing down. It holds two datasets of letters in its one department, Patient Records. A dataset is the platform’s name for a registered, named collection of records. The platform calls the clinic harbour on screen. Dunmore is the data custodian of Patient Records, which means that Dunmore is the person the department trusts to decide who may read its data.

1
Dunmore
Dunmore opens the page about closing down the organisation
Munitas console · Closing down the organisation · /closing

Closing down an organisation means ending its use of Munitas in stages, and the page explains the three stages before it offers anything. In the first stage, called Closing down and 15 days long, the clinic takes no changes but its people can still read, and a data custodian can cancel. In the second stage, called Closed to its people and also 15 days long, nobody in the clinic can do anything. In the third, everything inside the clinic is deleted, unless a legal hold stands over it. A legal hold is an order to keep records, and it appears in part four.

Under Where harbour stands a green Open label says The organisation is running normally. The one button is the red Close down this organisation, with a line below it naming who may press it: a data custodian of the organisation, or a platform administrator.
2
Dunmore
Dunmore writes down why the clinic is closing down
Munitas console · Closing down the organisation · the Close down harbour? box

Pressing the button opens a box that asks for a reason before anything happens. The reason is stored with the closing down and is shown to everybody in the clinic afterwards, so that nobody has to guess why the organisation was closed. Nothing is deleted by this step.

The box is titled “Close down harbour?” and repeats the three stages in one paragraph. The reason field reads “Harbour Clinic is winding down. The last patient was seen on 30 September.” and the red Close it down button is now usable.
3
Dunmore
The clinic is now closing down, and Dunmore can still cancel
Munitas console · Closing down the organisation · /closing

The status changes from Open to Closing down. From this moment the clinic takes no changes: nothing can be added, registered or approved, because a write of any kind is refused by the database. Reading still works until the first date. Because this is the first stage, the page offers Dunmore a button to cancel.

A yellow banner across the top reads This organisation is closing down and gives Oct 26, 2026 (15 days left) as the last day to cancel, with the time of day after it. The status box says Closing down started on Oct 11, 2026, asked for by Dunmore, and names Nov 10, 2026 as the day everything inside is deleted. The Cancel the closing down button is there, and a notice at the bottom right reads harbour is closing down.
PART TWO

An ordinary member can read, and cannot stop it

Quinn is an analyst at Harbour Clinic. An analyst is a person who works with data. The role carries no say over who may read the clinic’s data and none over the clinic itself.

4
Quinn
Quinn sees the same yellow banner on the home page
Munitas console · Home · /

Everybody in the clinic is told that it is being closed, not only the person who started it. Quinn has no menu entry for closing down, because that entry is shown only to data custodians, data protection officers and platform administrators. The banner carries a link instead.

The banner reads This organisation is closing down with the same last day to cancel, Oct 26, 2026, and ends with a link See where it stands. At the bottom of the menu the role is Analyst and the clinic is marked closing down.
5
Quinn
Quinn presses Cancel the closing down and is refused
Munitas console · Closing down the organisation · /closing

Quinn follows the link and reaches the status page, which shows the same Cancel the closing down button. The page draws the button for everybody, because the platform decides when it is pressed and not the page. The platform checks the role against its access rules and answers with the reason.

A red panel under the button reads Could not cancel the closing down, and gives one reason: only a data custodian of the organisation, or a platform administrator, may cancel its closing down. Nothing on the page has changed, and the status still reads Closing down.
PART THREE

Fifteen days pass, and nobody in the clinic can do anything

Nobody cancelled. Fifteen days is too long to wait. At each jump in time a small script run by an administrator moved the clinic’s two closing dates back, and changed nothing else. The platform works out where the clinic stands from those two dates every time it is asked, so moving them is all that a clock moving on would change. For that reason the dates on the screens after a jump are earlier than they would be on a real calendar.

6
Dunmore
Dunmore signs in and finds a notice instead of the usual screens
Munitas console · Closing notice · shown in place of every other screen

The first stage has ended, so the clinic is now in the second stage, called Closed to its people. The platform refuses every request from the clinic’s people from this point, including the request to cancel. The console therefore shows one notice and nothing else, instead of a menu whose every link would be refused.

The heading reads harbour has closed down to its people, with a red Closed to its people label. The status line reads The time to cancel ended on Oct 10, 2026. Everything inside is deleted on Oct 26, 2026 (15 days left), which are earlier dates than before because of the clock move described above. The only control is Sign out.
PART FOUR

A platform administrator records a legal hold

A law firm, Aldous and Brennan LLP, has written to the platform. A patient is making a claim against Harbour Clinic and the firm asks that the clinic’s records be kept. An instruction like this is called a legal hold. It arrives in writing, outside the platform, and goes to a platform administrator. A platform administrator is a person who runs Munitas itself, and who has no say over who may read any department’s data. Priya is one.

7
Priya
Priya sees every organisation and where each one stands
Munitas console · Closing down the organisation · /closing, the table of every organisation

A platform administrator sees the clinic as one row of a table that covers every organisation. The table shows dates and states only, and never what an organisation holds. Harbour Clinic is already in the second stage.

The row for harbour reads Closed to its people in red, with Deleted on Oct 26, 2026 and None under Legal hold. The rows for finance and health read Open and each carries a Close down button.
8
Priya
Priya copies the notice into the form
Munitas console · Legal holds · /legal-holds, Record a legal hold

The form asks for every part of the notice: which organisation it applies to, who issued it, the issuer’s own reference, a contact, what triggered it, the date it arrived, what the matter is about, and what must be kept. It also asks for a temporary custodian, which is the person who answers for the kept records while the hold stands. Priya names Adeyemi, the clinic’s data protection officer, a person who watches how the clinic handles personal data. The form will not send until every required part is filled in.

The fields read: organisation harbour, temporary custodian Adeyemi, matter Alder v Harbour Clinic, matter number HC-2026-0417, issued by Aldous and Brennan LLP, for the claimant, reference AB/2026/17, and what must be kept Every record of the claimant, and the audit trail of who read them. The two date fields for the range of records are optional and left empty.
9
Priya
The hold is recorded, and it waits for a second administrator
Munitas console · Legal holds · Waiting for a second administrator

The hold does not take effect yet, because one platform administrator alone cannot place it. It already stops the clinic being deleted, though. The reason is that a deletion could otherwise happen between the moment the hold is recorded and the moment it is approved, and the hold would then have protected nothing. If nobody approves it within 7 days, it lapses and stops standing in the way.

A card titled HC-2026-0417: Alder v Harbour Clinic carries an amber label Waiting for a second administrator. It repeats every part of the notice, reads Recorded by Priya on Oct 11, 2026, and under Lapses if not approved by gives Oct 18, 2026 as the day it lapses if nobody approves it. Under the buttons: You recorded this one, so a different administrator approves it.
10
Priya
Priya presses Approve on the hold that Priya recorded, and is refused
Munitas console · Legal holds · Waiting for a second administrator

The page offers the Approve button to every platform administrator and the platform decides when it is pressed. It refuses an approval from the person who recorded the hold. The same rule is also written into the database as a check, so a fault in the program could not bypass it.

A red panel reads Could not decide this hold and gives the reason a legal hold is approved by a different platform administrator from the one who placed it. The hold card above it is unchanged.
PART FIVE

A second platform administrator approves it

Ravi is the second platform administrator. Ravi and Priya hold the same role, and the rule is only that the two are different people.

11
Ravi
Ravi reads the notice and writes a note
Munitas console · Legal holds · Waiting for a second administrator

Ravi sees the same waiting hold, with every part of the notice in front of the decision. The note is stored with the decision, and a note is required only when a hold is declined. Ravi writes down what was checked.

The signed-in name at the bottom left of the menu is Ravi, a Platform administrator. The note field reads Notice checked against the issuing firm’s reference. Both Approve it and Decline are offered, and there is no line saying that Ravi recorded this one.
12
Ravi
The hold is in force
Munitas console · Legal holds · In force

Approving moves the card from the waiting list to the list of holds in force. While it stands, nothing inside the clinic is deleted, whatever the dates say. A hold in force has a review date, so that somebody has to look at it again and it does not stand by default for ever. Releasing it is possible only with a written reason.

The card now carries a red label In force and reads Approved by Ravi on Oct 11, 2026: “Notice checked against the issuing firm’s reference.” and Review by Jan 8, 2027. The line Adeyemi, has not acknowledged it yet shows that the temporary custodian has not responded. Below the card the button Release this hold says that releasing starts the closing period again.
PART SIX

The temporary custodian acknowledges the hold

Adeyemi is the clinic’s data protection officer and has been named as the temporary custodian of the held records. The clinic is in its closing stage, so the usual screens are closed to Adeyemi too. The one thing still open is the hold that names Adeyemi.

13
Adeyemi
Adeyemi is told that a hold names Adeyemi as custodian
Munitas console · Closing notice · shown in place of every other screen

Besides the closing status, the notice shows a second box for the legal hold. It names the issuing firm, the matter and what must be kept. The temporary custodian is accountable for the records while the hold stands, and confirms having read the notice by pressing the button.

The status line now ends A legal hold is in force, so nothing will be deleted while it stands. A second box is headed A legal hold names you as custodian and holds the dark button I have read it and will answer for these records.
14
Adeyemi
Adeyemi acknowledges the hold
Munitas console · Closing notice · shown in place of every other screen

The acknowledgement is stored with the hold and shown to the platform administrators. Only the named person can give it. Another member of the clinic who pressed the same button would be refused.

The button has been replaced by a green line, You acknowledged this hold on Oct 11, 2026.
PART SEVEN

The time is up, and the hold stands

The second period ends. Fifteen days is too long to wait. At each jump in time a small script run by an administrator moved the clinic’s two closing dates back, and changed nothing else. The platform works out where the clinic stands from those two dates every time it is asked, so moving them is all that a clock moving on would change. For that reason the dates on the screens after a jump are earlier than they would be on a real calendar.

15
Priya
Both periods have ended, and nothing is deleted
Munitas console · Closing down the organisation · /closing, the table of every organisation

Every few minutes the platform runs a sweep, which is a check for organisations whose time is up. It deletes an organisation only when both periods have ended and no legal hold stands. A sweep ran after the dates moved, and it deleted nothing, because the hold is in force.

The row for harbour reads Held, time is up in amber, with Not deleted while the hold stands as the next date and In force under Legal hold.
PART EIGHT

The matter ends, and the hold is released

The law firm confirms in writing that the matter is settled.

16
Ravi
Ravi releases the hold and writes down why
Munitas console · Legal holds · the Release box

Releasing a hold means that the records are no longer protected by it. The box says so, and it asks for a written reason, which is stored with the hold. Releasing does not delete anything by itself, and the platform starts the second period again from the moment of release, so a release made by mistake still leaves 15 days to notice.

The box is titled Release HC-2026-0417?. The reason reads Matter settled. Written confirmation received from Aldous and Brennan LLP, and the red Release it button is usable.
17
Ravi
The closing period starts again
Munitas console · Closing down the organisation · /closing, the table of every organisation

The clinic is back in the second stage, with a new deletion date 15 days after the release. No hold stands, so the sweep will delete the clinic when that date arrives.

The row for harbour reads Closed to its people in red, with Deleted on Oct 26, 2026 and None under Legal hold. The date matches the 15 days that the release added.
PART NINE

Nothing stands in the way, and the clinic is deleted

The second period ends again. Fifteen days is too long to wait. At each jump in time a small script run by an administrator moved the clinic’s two closing dates back, and changed nothing else. The platform works out where the clinic stands from those two dates every time it is asked, so moving them is all that a clock moving on would change. For that reason the dates on the screens after a jump are earlier than they would be on a real calendar.

18
Priya
Harbour Clinic is deleted, and a short record is kept
Munitas console · Legal holds · Deleted organisations

The sweep deletes everything inside the clinic: its datasets, its sealed versions, its departments, its people and its stored files. A sealed version is a dataset state that can never be edited, and the platform allows its deletion only inside a purge that the database itself has confirmed as due, so nothing else can be removed this way. The clinic’s sign-in accounts are removed too, so nobody can sign in as a person of the clinic any more. Two things stay. One is a short record, which names no contact detail and holds none of the clinic’s records. The other is the audit trail, the list of who was allowed to read what, which is kept for seven years and then removed. Both are filed under a new name made from the old one, so that a later organisation can be called harbour again.

Under Deleted organisations the entry for harbour begins with the line Filed under and the new name, which starts with harbour~deleted-. It then reads Closing down was asked for by Dunmore on Oct 11, 2026, because: Harbour Clinic is winding down, Removed 3 sign-in accounts, and 2 audit rows of who read what are kept until Oct 11, 2033, and then removed. The last line, Legal holds that applied: HC-2026-0417 (Aldous and Brennan LLP, for the claimant, released), shows the hold by its number and issuer.
